description:
FILED s470by (Opus, 2026-09-06) while taking the #1300 SHOW_SBCL bar.

CLAUDE.md Quick Reference says `PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1 <any runner>` prints the exact
command it spawns, and names FIVE runners (the gate, the sweep, the perl suite,
./runpcl, tools/pclperl-for-tests).  `pcl` -- the user-facing command, and since
#1300 the one that also answers --version and --cache-info -- is a SIXTH
SBCL-spawning entry point, and it is the odd one out: it prints its command line
under `-v` / `--verbose` only.

MEASURED (this tree, 2026-09-06):
    PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1 ./pcl -e 1          # prints NOTHING
    ./pcl -v -e 1                       # prints "pcl: exec sbcl --core ..."
    PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1 ./runpcl prog.pl    # prints "SBCL[runpcl]: sbcl --core ..."

Not a semantics bug and not a violation of the five-runner claim (pcl is not one
of the five), so it was FILED rather than folded into #1300's batch: a one-line
change is still a change, and it would have cost that batch a second full gate.

FIX (one line, `pcl` ~211):
    say STDERR "pcl: exec @cmd" if $verbose || $ENV{PCL_SHOW_SBCL};
GUARD: a row in Pl/t/cache-surface-01.t asserting that `PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1 pcl -e 1`
prints a line naming the core, beside the existing --cache-info rows.
subject: pcl is the one SBCL-spawning entry point that ignores PCL_SHOW_SBCL (it prints its command line under -v only) -- one line, filed rather than folded into #1300 so that batch would not owe a second gate
